hunks.baseline: Jin Wikyung spoke to me as I stared fixedly at the Quest Window.
hunks.sol: Jin Wikyung spoke as I stared fixedly at the Quest Window.

hunks.baseline: “You look very tired.”
hunks.sol: “You must be exhausted.”

hunks.baseline: Tired? I was amazed that my current state of mind could be summed up in such a simple word.
hunks.sol: Exhausted? I was amazed that my current state of mind could be summed up in such a simple word.

hunks.baseline: Instead of answering, I looked at the steaming teacup.
hunks.sol: Instead of answering, I stared at the steaming teacup.

hunks.baseline: I had done my best, but I couldn’t stop the war. The family council had turned into a war council, and with the Head Elder’s full support, Jin Wikyung had taken up command without hesitation.
hunks.sol: I had done my best, but I hadn’t been able to stop the war. The family council had turned into a war council, and with the Head Elder’s full support, Jin Wikyung had taken command without hesitation.

hunks.baseline: At dawn, dozens of messenger pigeons took to the sky while messengers rode hard on horseback. A tight security net was thrown over the entire area.
hunks.sol: Around daybreak, dozens of messenger pigeons took to the sky and messengers rode hard on horseback. A tight security net spread across the area.

hunks.baseline: When the family council finally broke up in that tense atmosphere, Jin Wikyung, Wipeng, and I moved to the Lesser Family Head’s office.
hunks.sol: When the family council finally broke up amid that tense atmosphere, Jin Wikyung, Wipeng, and I moved to the Lesser Family Head’s office.

hunks.baseline: I felt like crying at Jin Wikyung’s warm words. Not because I was moved, but because it felt so unfair.
hunks.sol: Jin Wikyung’s warm words almost brought tears to my eyes. Not because I was moved, but because I felt so wronged.

hunks.baseline: And since we were on the subject, why the hell did that “bound to happen someday” have to happen now?
hunks.sol: And while we were on the subject, why the hell did that “bound to happen someday” have to happen now?

hunks.baseline: While I was fuming inwardly, Wipeng suddenly spoke.
hunks.sol: While I fumed inwardly, Wipeng suddenly spoke.

hunks.baseline: “Why?”
hunks.sol: “What is it?”

hunks.baseline: “The Head Elder… I simply cannot figure out what he’s thinking.”
hunks.sol: “The Head Elder… I simply cannot fathom his intentions.”

hunks.baseline: The Head Elder. The moment I heard that name, I abandoned all other thoughts. He was the most unsettling person among the NPCs I had encountered in this game.
hunks.sol: The Head Elder. The instant I heard that name, every other thought vanished. Of all the NPCs I had encountered in this game, he was the most unsettling.

hunks.baseline: He seemed genuinely devoted to the family, yet he also gave off the unmistakable air of a politician maneuvering for his own benefit.
hunks.sol: At times, he seemed genuinely devoted to the family. At others, he reeked of a politician maneuvering for his own benefit.

hunks.baseline: I cautiously opened my mouth.
“What kind of person is the Head Elder?”
hunks.sol: I cautiously asked, “What kind of person is the Head Elder?”

hunks.baseline: “He is a martial artist of a high realm, and his schemes run deep. You could call him one of the most dangerous types of people in Murim.”
hunks.sol: “He is a martial artist of a high realm, and his schemes run deep. You could call him one of the most dangerous kinds of people in Murim.”

hunks.baseline: “That dangerous?”
hunks.sol: “He’s that dangerous?”

hunks.baseline: Jin Wikyung nodded heavily.
hunks.sol: Jin Wikyung nodded gravely.

hunks.baseline: “Even the other Elders are little more than the Head Elder’s hands and feet. He rarely reveals himself, yet he has used the Elder Council to win over influential members and bring them under his command. He has been doing so for decades.”
hunks.sol: “Even the other Elders are little more than the Head Elder’s hands and feet. He rarely shows himself, yet he has used the Council of Elders as his limbs to win over influential members and draw them under his command. He has been doing so for decades.”

hunks.baseline: “We cannot know the exact truth, but he must have an ulterior motive. Of that, I am certain.”
hunks.sol: “We cannot know for certain, but he must have some ulterior motive. Of that, I am sure.”

hunks.baseline: I had felt the same way. But that had merely been the Head Elder’s clever way of speaking—a suggestion that perhaps we should back down at this point.
hunks.sol: I had felt the same way. But that had merely been the Head Elder’s clever way of suggesting that we should back down.

hunks.baseline: If Jin Wikyung had pretended to be insane and accepted that proposal, the result would have been obvious.
hunks.sol: If Jin Wikyung had thrown caution to the wind and accepted his proposal, the result would have been obvious.

hunks.baseline: “A bloodbath would have broken out.”
hunks.sol: “A bloodbath would have followed.”

hunks.baseline: The Jin Family of Taiyuan’s leadership would have split in two and continued fighting until they killed one another. If we lost, we would die. Even if we won, we would suffer tremendous damage.
hunks.sol: The Jin Family of Taiyuan’s leadership would have split in two and fought until they killed one another. If we lost, we would die. Even if we won, we would suffer tremendous losses.

hunks.baseline: A chill ran down my spine at the thought. It fit the image I had formed of him perfectly.
hunks.sol: The thought sent a chill down my spine. It fit the image I had formed of him perfectly.

hunks.baseline: A politician like a hyena, stepping back and waiting for his moment.
hunks.sol: A hyena of a politician, stepping back and waiting for his moment.

hunks.baseline: Jin Wikyung tilted his teacup.
hunks.sol: Jin Wikyung took a sip of tea.

hunks.baseline: “But that is only a guess. We do not know what the Head Elder truly intends. He is still one of the family’s elders, and a powerful ally. Be wary of him, but do not make an enemy of him. For now, we need to overcome the situation rather than distrust everyone around us.”
hunks.sol: “But that is only speculation. We do not know what the Head Elder truly intends. He is still a senior of our family and a powerful ally. Be wary of him, but do not make an enemy of him. Right now, we must focus on overcoming this crisis rather than distrusting the people around us.”

hunks.baseline: He was telling me to look at the forest, not the trees.
hunks.sol: He was telling me to see the forest, not the trees.

hunks.baseline: The problem was that the forest itself wasn’t exactly in good shape, either.
hunks.sol: The problem was, the forest itself wasn’t exactly in good shape.

hunks.baseline: As if he had read my thoughts, Wipeng brought up the subject.
hunks.sol: As if he had read my thoughts, Wipeng brought up that very subject.

hunks.baseline: “The situation is not good, either. According to our outside sources, rumors that Lee Seogeun was poisoned to death have begun spreading, and the main family’s reputation is falling.”
hunks.sol: “The situation is grim as well. According to our outside sources, rumors that Lee Seogeun was poisoned to death are spreading, and our family’s reputation is plummeting.”

hunks.baseline: “Yes. All of Shanxi is in an uproar over it.”
hunks.sol: “Yes. All of Shanxi Province is in an uproar.”

hunks.baseline: There was no internet here, and yet rumors had already spread across this vast land. It was certainly strange.
hunks.sol: There was no internet here, yet the rumor had already spread across this vast land. Something was clearly wrong.

hunks.baseline: Who could it be? A third faction? A staged act by the Mount Heng Sword Sect?
hunks.sol: Who could it be? A third faction? A scheme staged by the Mount Heng Sword Sect itself?

hunks.baseline: I hoped it was the latter if possible. Nothing was more dangerous than an enemy who remained unseen.
hunks.sol: I hoped it was the latter. Nothing was more dangerous than an enemy who remained unseen.

hunks.baseline: “The people are still taking the rumors with a grain of salt, but the other sects…”
hunks.sol: “The public still seems unsure what to believe, but the other sects…”

hunks.baseline: Immediately after obtaining the information about Lee Seogeun’s poisoning, Jin Wikyung had sent requests for support to the other small and mid-sized sects in Shanxi. But it seemed every one of them had failed.
hunks.sol: As soon as Jin Wikyung learned of Lee Seogeun’s poisoning, he had sent requests for aid to the other small and mid-sized sects in Shanxi Province. Apparently, every last one of them had come to nothing.

hunks.baseline: *This keeps getting worse.*
hunks.sol: *This just keeps getting worse.*

hunks.baseline: I was looking out the window, thinking that, when—
hunks.sol: I was staring out the window, thinking that, when—

hunks.baseline: A pigeon landed on the windowsill with the sound of beating wings.
hunks.sol: A pigeon landed on the windowsill with a flutter of wings.

hunks.baseline: “…It looks like a reply has arrived?”
hunks.sol: “…Looks like we got a reply.”

hunks.baseline: As the carriage approached the grand signboard written in magnificent calligraphy and the martial artists standing guard at the main gate with a stern aura, the coachman loosened the reins.
hunks.sol: As the carriage approached the grand signboard emblazoned with majestic calligraphy and the martial artists guarding the main gate with stern auras, the coachman slackened the reins.

hunks.baseline: “Stop. State your identity and purpose!”
hunks.sol: “Stop! State your identity and purpose!”

hunks.baseline: The gate guard called out loudly and blocked the carriage. Given the circumstances, there was tension in his voice.
hunks.sol: The gate guard called out loudly as he moved to block the carriage. Given the circumstances, tension filled his voice.

hunks.baseline: More than that—
hunks.sol: And there was something else.

hunks.baseline: *This isn’t ordinary.*
hunks.sol: *They’re no ordinary visitors.*

hunks.baseline: The coachman holding the reins gave off the unmistakable air of a trained martial artist, while the four-horse carriage had both luxury and dignity.
hunks.sol: The coachman holding the reins gave off the unmistakable air of a trained martial artist, while the four-horse carriage was both lavish and dignified.

hunks.baseline: *But why does he look familiar?*
hunks.sol: *But why do they look familiar?*

hunks.baseline: The coachman, too. The carriage, too. Where had he seen them?
hunks.sol: The coachman and the carriage alike. Where had he seen them before?

hunks.baseline: The question vanished the moment he saw the coachman’s sharp eyes. That aura, that gaze. This was certainly no ordinary visitor.
hunks.sol: The question vanished the moment he met the coachman’s sharp gaze. That aura, those eyes. These were certainly no ordinary guests.

hunks.baseline: The carriage door opened, and a red silk slipper stepped lightly onto the ground.
hunks.sol: The carriage door opened, and a red silk slipper touched lightly to the ground.

hunks.baseline: The gate guard’s eyes grew dazed. He wasn’t the only one. Everyone who saw the woman reacted the same way.
hunks.sol: The gate guard’s eyes went glassy. He wasn’t the only one. Everyone who saw the woman reacted the same way.

hunks.baseline: A vacant voice escaped the gate guard’s mouth.
hunks.sol: A dazed murmur escaped his lips.

hunks.baseline: The woman, Wolhwa, answered with a charming smile.
hunks.sol: The woman—Wolhwa—answered with a bewitching smile.

hunks.baseline: “Hmm. I’m here to collect an unpaid tab?”
hunks.sol: “Hmm. To collect an unpaid tab?”

hunks.baseline: I froze halfway to standing.
hunks.sol: I froze halfway to my feet.

hunks.baseline: A face I could never forget. And a face that had no business being here.
hunks.sol: A face I could never forget. And one that had no business being here.

hunks.baseline: The first NPC I had met in this game. A courtesan at Honghwaru—and my, Jin Taekyung’s, girl. You know.
hunks.sol: The first NPC I had met in this game. A courtesan at Honghwaru and my—Jin Taekyung’s—pinky.[^1] That thing.

hunks.baseline: *Why is noona coming out of there…?*
hunks.sol: *Noona, what are you doing here…?*

hunks.baseline: “You remember me after all. Our Young Master Jin.”
hunks.sol: “So you do remember me. Our Young Master Jin.”

hunks.baseline: Wolhwa giggled. She was beautiful, had a beautiful laugh, and when a beautiful woman laughed, she became even more beautiful…
hunks.sol: Wolhwa giggled. She was pretty, her laugh was pretty, and when a pretty girl laughed, she looked even prettier…

hunks.baseline: I whispered in a tightly restrained voice.
hunks.sol: I whispered in a hushed voice.

hunks.baseline: “What brings you here? No, never mind. Leave. Get out.”
hunks.sol: “What are you doing here? No, forget it. Leave. Get out.”

hunks.baseline: I nudged Wolhwa with my elbow.
hunks.sol: I nudged Wolhwa repeatedly with my elbow.

hunks.baseline: Of all times, she had to show up in this atmosphere.
hunks.sol: Of all times, she had to show up now.

hunks.baseline: The entire family was on high alert. If word got out that I had called for a courtesan, I couldn’t even imagine what would happen to my reputation. Just thinking about it made my vision swim.
hunks.sol: The entire family was on high alert. If word got around that I had summoned a courtesan, I couldn’t even imagine what would happen to my reputation. Just thinking about it made me dizzy.

hunks.baseline: “Don’t poke me. That tickles.”
hunks.sol: “Stop poking me. It tickles.”

hunks.baseline: “I know, so get out quickly. There are other people here. What are you trying to do by suddenly coming here? We’re expecting an important guest, too.”
hunks.sol: “Fine, so hurry up and leave. There are other people here. What are you trying to pull, barging in all of a sudden? We’re expecting an important guest, too.”

hunks.baseline: The timing was damn awful, too. I was waiting for a guest from a sect called the Lower District Sect in the Lesser Family Head’s office.
hunks.sol: The timing was goddamn awful. I was in the Lesser Family Head’s office, waiting for a guest from a sect called the Lower District Sect.

hunks.baseline: “Ah, it’s not what you think. I didn’t call her. She’s leaving now, too. Right?”
hunks.sol: “Ah, it’s not what you think. I didn’t call her. She says she’s leaving now. Right?”

hunks.baseline: “Our Young Master Jin is still so adorable. But you guessed wrong. I came here because I have business to attend to.”
hunks.sol: “Our Young Master Jin is as adorable as ever. But you’ve got it wrong. I came here on business.”

hunks.baseline: “Don’t call me ‘our Young Master Jin.’ I’m going to live chastely from today onward. I don’t have any business with you anymore, so get out quickly.”
hunks.sol: “Hey, none of that ‘our Young Master Jin’ stuff. I’m going to live chastely from today onward. I won’t have any business with your side anymore, so hurry up and leave.”

hunks.baseline: In desperation, I grabbed Wolhwa around the waist and hoisted her up—
hunks.sol: In desperation, I wrapped my arms around Wolhwa’s waist and hoisted her up—

hunks.baseline: What the hell? Why won’t she lift?
hunks.sol: What the hell? Why couldn’t I lift her?

hunks.baseline: Wolhwa looked slender, but was she so big-boned that she weighed a lot?
hunks.sol: Wolhwa looked slender, but was she so big-boned that she weighed a ton?

hunks.baseline: What was my Strength stat again? With pure physical strength alone, I could grind a rock into powder. And yet I couldn’t lift one female NPC, which meant—
hunks.sol: How high was my Strength stat? With pure physical strength alone, I could grind a rock into powder. And yet I couldn’t lift one female NPC, which meant—

hunks.baseline: I ignored Jin Wikyung’s second call and furtively let go. Then I heightened my Qi Sense.
hunks.sol: Ignoring Jin Wikyung’s second call, I furtively let go and heightened my Qi Sense.

hunks.baseline: “Ahahahahaha! This is driving me insane!”
hunks.sol: “Ahahahahaha! I can’t take this!”

hunks.baseline: As Wolhwa laughed herself to death, a Level Window appeared above her head. At the same time, I heard Jin Wikyung call my name for the third time.
hunks.sol: As Wolhwa howled with laughter, a Level Window appeared above her head. At the same time, Jin Wikyung called my name for the third time.

hunks.baseline: She was different from how she had acted until now. Every movement carried the grace and elegance of a noblewoman.
hunks.sol: She was completely different from how she had acted until now. Every movement carried the grace and elegance of a noblewoman.

hunks.baseline: I kept my mouth shut like mute Samryong,[^1] and Wolhwa flashed me a grin.
hunks.sol: I kept my mouth shut like mute Samryong,[^2] and Wolhwa gave me a broad grin.

hunks.baseline: *Don’t talk to me. Please don’t.*
hunks.sol: *Don’t talk to me. Please.*

hunks.baseline: “It seems I haven’t been introduced to one person.”
hunks.sol: “It seems there is still one person I haven’t been introduced to.”

hunks.baseline: I opened my mouth with a feeling like I was coughing up blood.
hunks.sol: Feeling as though I were coughing up blood, I forced myself to speak.

hunks.baseline: “Yes. I hope we get along too, Young Master Jin.”
hunks.sol: “Yes. I look forward to getting along with you too, Young Master Jin.”

hunks.baseline: With a cough, Jin Wikyung glanced at me.
hunks.sol: Jin Wikyung coughed and glanced at me.

hunks.baseline: “He is a regular at our establishment—the Honghwaru in Taiyuan. It also serves as this sect’s Shanxi branch.”
hunks.sol: “He’s a regular at our establishment—the Honghwaru in Taiyuan. It also serves as our sect’s Shanxi branch.”

hunks.baseline: I avoided everyone’s gaze. Wolhwa let out a burst of laughter, then brought up the real subject.
hunks.sol: I avoided everyone’s eyes. Wolhwa stifled a laugh, then got down to business.

hunks.baseline: I had felt it several times before, but she really was a refreshingly direct woman. Jin Wikyung and Wipeng also turned their attention away from me and joined the conversation.
hunks.sol: I had noticed it several times before, but she really was a straightforward woman. Jin Wikyung and Wipeng finally took their eyes off me and focused on the conversation.

hunks.baseline: Wolhwa smiled sweetly at Jin Wikyung’s question.
hunks.sol: Wolhwa smiled at Jin Wikyung’s question.

hunks.baseline: “The reason… I will tell you if necessary. First, we are doing this for our sect’s benefit.”
hunks.sol: “The reason… If you must know, I’ll tell you. First, we are doing this for our sect’s benefit.”

hunks.baseline: “Benefit. What specific compensation do you want?”
hunks.sol: “Benefit. What compensation do you seek?”

hunks.baseline: “Good.”
hunks.sol: “Agreed.”

hunks.baseline: Wolhwa also looked slightly surprised.
hunks.sol: Even Wolhwa looked slightly surprised.

hunks.baseline: “You decide quickly.”
hunks.sol: “That was quick.”

hunks.baseline: “Because I have staked everything the family has.”
hunks.sol: “I have wagered everything our family has.”

hunks.baseline: “I am the Lesser Family Head, and with Father absent, I possess the authority of the acting Family Head.”
hunks.sol: “I am the Lesser Family Head. With Father absent, I hold the authority of the acting Family Head.”

hunks.baseline: “I hear the internal opposition is quite fierce. The Elder Council, for example?”
hunks.sol: “I hear the opposition within your family is considerable. The Council of Elders, for example?”

hunks.baseline: “As expected of the Lower District Sect. Your information is fast.”
hunks.sol: “As expected of the Lower District Sect. Your information travels fast.”

hunks.baseline: “It cannot be helped. Information is essential for survival in this bleak Murim. We need skills like these to make a living, don’t we?”
hunks.sol: “It cannot be helped. Information is essential if one hopes to survive in this harsh Murim. We need at least this much savvy to make a living, don’t we?”

hunks.baseline: Watching Wolhwa smile, I suddenly had a thought.
hunks.sol: As I watched Wolhwa smile, a thought suddenly occurred to me.

hunks.baseline: *That information. Did I—or rather, did Jin Taekyung—let it slip?*
hunks.sol: *That information. Did I—or rather, did Jin Taekyung—leak it?*

hunks.baseline: I had wondered where I had heard the name Lower District Sect before. It was an information-gathering sect that appeared regularly in martial-arts novels. In other words, Wolhwa, its Branch Leader, was a veteran information merchant.
hunks.sol: I had been wondering where I had heard the name Lower District Sect before. It was one of those information-gathering sects that appeared all the time in martial-arts novels. In other words, Wolhwa, its Branch Leader, was a veteran information broker.

hunks.baseline: On top of that, she was an outstanding martial artist at Level 50. A woman like that had disguised herself as a courtesan to meet a guy like Jin Taekyung?
hunks.sol: On top of that, she was an outstanding Level 50 martial artist. A woman like her had disguised herself as a courtesan to meet a guy like Jin Taekyung?

hunks.baseline: Her beauty was dazzling enough to make me wonder if a goddess had descended. Whenever she smiled, roses came to mind. Only now could I see the sharp thorns hidden beneath all that splendor.
hunks.sol: She was dazzling enough to make me wonder if a goddess had descended from heaven. Every time she smiled, I thought of a rose. Only now could I see the sharp thorns hidden beneath all that splendor.

hunks.baseline: Jin Wikyung spoke with a stiff expression.
hunks.sol: Jin Wikyung spoke, his expression stiff.
[^1]: In Korea, a raised pinky can refer to someone’s girlfriend or mistress.

hunks.baseline: [^1]: Samryong is the mute protagonist of a well-known Korean short story; his name literally means “Three Dragons.”
hunks.sol: [^2]: Samryong is the mute protagonist of a well-known Korean short story; his name literally means “Three Dragons.”
